draft.title: Geospatial technologies
card: GPS
The global positioning system uses signals from satellites to work out where a receiver is on Earth. A phone or a car navigation unit can use it to show your position.
Satellite images
Satellites orbiting Earth take pictures of the land and sea from above. Comparing images taken at different times shows change, such as a bushfire scar or a growing suburb.
GIS

A geographic information system (GIS) stores information about places in separate layers, such as roads, rivers and houses. The layers can be switched on and off and placed over each other on one map.
Layering lets geographers see how things relate. A GIS map of flood areas over a map of houses can show which homes are close to a river.
draft.remember: GPS finds position, satellite images show the land from above, and GIS layers information to show patterns.

a.q: What does a geographic information system (GIS) do?
opts: Layers information about places on one map
Gives the position of a receiver using satellites
Takes pictures of Earth from space
Shows the height of land using lines
a.why: A GIS stores information in layers that can be combined on one map. GPS is the tool that uses satellite signals to find a position, which is the most tempting wrong option.

b.q: A council in Bendigo wants to know which homes are close to a creek that floods. Which tool would help most?
opts: A GIS with layers for homes and flood areas
A GPS receiver to find the position of the creek
A single satellite image taken last year
A compass to find the direction of the creek
b.why: A GIS can place a layer of flood areas over a layer of homes, so the council can see which homes are close to the creek. A satellite image shows the land, but it does not store separate layers that can be combined.
b.clue: Which tool can place one set of information over another?

a.best: Layers information about places on one map

b.best: A GIS with layers for homes and flood areas

problems.detail: The clue 'Think about the word layers' gives the answer away. Only the right option contains the word 'Layers', so a student can match the word without knowing what a GIS does.

a.q: Ava places a map of roads over a map of rivers on a computer, then switches the roads off again. Which technology is she using?
opts: A geographic information system
The global positioning system
A satellite image of the area
A compass and a north arrow
a.why: A GIS stores information in separate layers that can be placed over each other and switched on and off. GPS is the most tempting wrong option, but it only uses satellite signals to work out a position.
a.clue: Which tool can combine and hide different sets of information?
